title: Scrim owners and coverage runbook — May 2029
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, ad-hoc tracker ('scrim runbook') to map short-lived coverage and owner responsibilities for cross-functional micro-sprints and surge windows. Intended for quick handoffs, weekend/holiday surge planning, and 48–72h experiments where we need clear contact points but don’t want to create formal rotation artifacts.

How to use this sheet (quick):
- Use rows below to register coverage commitments for the next 7–14 days.
- Update the "Last checked" column each time you confirm availability.
- If you take ownership for a row, ping the listed stakeholders in the linked Slack thread and tag the ticket (if relevant).
- This doc is schema-lite: keep it short, update frequently.

Column headers (implicit): Route | Primary owner | Contact (email/phone) | Backup owner | Coverage window (UTC) | Expected SLA (p95) | Escalation path | Notes | Last checked

Rows (example entries):
1) Hosted-API / low-traffic ramp | Ethan Park | ethan@redwood.ai / +1-415-555-0191 | Priya Rao | 2029-05-04 08:00 – 2029-05-06 02:00 UTC | 250ms p95 | @oncall-platform -> SRE pager | Watch token burn and drop in token/sample latency; enable thin-batch if p95 > 400ms | 2029-05-09
2) Embeddings pipeline (bulk ingest) | Priya Rao | priya@redwood.ai | Carlos Mendes | 2029-05-05 22:00 – 2029-05-07 06:00 UTC | 800ms p95 for embedding calls | Ops lead -> infra oncall | Bulk job scheduled (JIRA-INF-1348); expect transient quota throttles; handoff to infra if throttled >10m | 2029-05-09
3) Dedicated pool validation (canary) | Carlos Mendes | carlos@redwood.ai | Riley Thompson | 2029-05-10 12:00 – 2029-05-10 20:00 UTC | 150ms p95 | Eng lead -> release-engineering | Running canary variant q4-8-bit; confirm fallback works | 2029-05-09
4) Private deploy partner trial | Riley Thompson | riley@redwood.ai | Maya Singh | 2029-05-09 00:00 – 2029-05-12 23:59 UTC | 500ms p95 | Customer success -> account exec | Partner is testing VPC egress rules; monitor connection flaps | 2029-05-09
5) Console telemetry sweep | Maya Singh | maya@redwood.ai | Ethan Park | 2029-05-08 09:00 – 2029-05-08 17:00 UTC | NA (data quality) | Analytics lead -> observability | Quick audit of tracing tags and cost breakdowns for last 48h; may toggle retention window | 2029-05-09

Quick escalation shortcuts: 
- Platform impact (hosted API significant latency or outage): @oncall-platform (pager) -> SRE lead -> Eng director
- Customer-facing incidents: @customer-success -> account exec -> product ops manager
- Billing/credits urgent: finance-ops channel and ops manager

Open action items (short):
- [ ] Ethan: confirm Eden token limits for the low-traffic ramp by 2029-05-11. Linked: JIRA-INF-1348.
- [ ] Priya + Carlos: run a single bulk ingest dry-run and post results in slack thread; mark outcome in Notes column.
- [ ] Riley: verify canary fallback by toggling model variant in staging and observing latency delta.
- [ ] Maya: update this sheet daily at 09:00 UTC during the coverage window; summarize top 3 risks each morning.

Notes and heuristics (for whoever inherits the row):
- Keep entries compact. If something grows beyond two lines of notes or more than one ticket, move to a proper runbook in Confluence and link it.
- Backups should be able to act within 30 minutes and have access to the same dashboards. If they don’t, add a pre-authorization note.
- When removing a row (coverage ended), append a 1–2 line postmortem summary in the Notes field and set Last checked to the removal date.

Change log (mini):
- 2029-05-03: Initial draft created (Maya Singh).
- 2029-05-05: Added embeddings pipeline entry and escalation path (Priya).
- 2029-05-09: Routine refresh and action items added (Maya).

If you are reading this and need a quick sync: ping @maya or drop a short note in slack:#prod-ops with the row number you want to claim.

End of runbook.
